question.worked_solution:
The range of $\sqrt[4]{x}$ is

$$
\sqrt[4]{x}\ge 0.
$$

Horizontal shifts and stretches do not affect the range. Hence,

$$
\sqrt[4]{2x-7}\ge 0.
$$

Multiplying the above inequality by $-3$ and then adding $2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[4]{2x-7} & \ge 0 \\ -3\sqrt[4]{2x-7} & \le 0 \\ -3\sqrt[4]{2x-7}+2 & \le 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the range of the given function is $f(x)\in (-\infty ,2].$

We can also see that this is true from the graph of the function. The graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown below.
